mappings.note: Explains checks and balances across the three organs and why they stop power being misused: the structure of government (LO-219) protecting citizens' rights (CG-SST3).
How executive and judiciary can answer an unfair law - feedback and judicial review: organs of government (LO-219) serving democratic accountability (CG-SST3).

Why a NOMINAL head such as the President can still influence a democracy: the office within the executive (LO-219) and its moral weight in the democratic order (CG-SST3). Unlike the purely motivational Kalam items, this one is about the office.
Why large nations adopt representative rather than direct democracy - a question about the form of democracy, so the goal.
Electing a class representative set beside electing MPs, and the principles common to both; the working of representative democracy, hence CG-SST3.
How grassroots democracy empowers ordinary citizens and why that matters: democratic processes at the local level (CG-SST3) and the local government's responsiveness (LO-219).
Demos and kratos giving 'rule of the people' - the meaning of democracy itself, so CG-SST3.
Why direct rule is impractical at scale; the short-answer form of the argument for representation.
The class representative as an illustration of representative democracy - a democratic principle drawn from school life, so CG-SST3.
What elected members do in an assembly - debate, persuade, decide: the legislature's working (LO-219) as a democratic process (CG-SST3).
Representative democracy as practised in India through MPs and MLAs; the form of democracy, hence CG-SST3.
Eighteen as the voting age - a constitutional provision governing the democratic process, so CG-SST3.
Defines grassroots democracy as ordinary citizens taking part in decisions that affect them, especially locally: CG-SST3's own phrase, with the local government's role (LO-219).
Why citizens should have a say in the laws that bind them - fairness, accountability and the will of the people, which is CG-SST3.
Why the three organs must work together for laws to be made, applied and interpreted; a point about how government functions, so LO-219.
The Mahabharata's rajanam dharmagoptaram analysed against modern good governance: an idea from an ancient system of thought (LO-225) applied to the rule of law (LO-219).
Vidhan Sabha as the state legislature - identifying an institution of the state tier, so LO-220.
The Governor as the state's nominal head; a state-tier office, hence LO-220.
Why rules are necessary for order and harmony - the ground of governance, so LO-219.
Separates governance as a process from government as the body that carries it out; the chapter's core distinction, under LO-219.
Digital transfers displacing money orders and bringing cybercrime with them - the change that forces new law-making, so LO-219.
The legislature's function of making and amending laws; an organ-to-function item, so LO-219.
The executive's role in carrying out laws and running administration - the companion item to the legislature question.
The judiciary interpreting laws, deciding breaches and reviewing actions; the third organ-to-function item, so LO-219.
Why separation of powers matters, namely to stop any one organ dominating - a structural point about government.
Defines a nominal head, illustrated by the President and a Governor: the executive's ceremonial office (LO-219) at two different tiers (LO-220).
Two Central Government responsibilities - defence and foreign affairs; the union tier's remit, so LO-220.
Two State Government responsibilities - police and public health; the state tier's remit, the counterpart of the Central item.
Dr Kalam as the 11th President (LO-220, an office of the union tier) and as the Missile Man of India's science programme (LO-224). The item asks for both.

A damaged item: the stem repeats the Kalam question but the answer given is about technology forcing the legislature to make new laws. Mapped on the content actually answered, which is the government's law-making role.
Judicial review as a guard against unjust or discriminatory laws: the judiciary's function (LO-219) upholding constitutional principle (CG-SST3).

Kalam's line on dreams turned towards active, accountable citizenship - the question explicitly asks about citizenship in a democracy, so CG-SST3. The other two Kalam items ask only for motivational recall and are left unmapped.
How the word cloud and the orderly-versus-chaotic traffic images set up rules, governance and order; the chapter's opening argument for government, so LO-219.
Cyber-fraud case assigning law-making, investigation and judgment to legislature, executive and judiciary - a sustained organ-to-function exercise, so LO-219.
Shopkeepers challenging a state trading-hours law: the organs that passed and can strike it down (LO-219), all within the state tier (LO-220).
A student council gathering grievances and putting them to management, named in the answer as representative democracy - so CG-SST3, as with the class-representative items.
Disaster response naming all three levels and the distinct part each played, and why they must coordinate - the clearest LO-220 item in the chapter.
